children: Our Bureau New Delhi: Japan's Suzuki Motor Corporation, the parent of India's largest carmaker Maruti Suzuki, plans to overhaul its manufacturing processes to halve vehicle development time by 2030, enabling it to bring new models to market faster.

Suzuki is targeting improving development efficiency by 30% compared with FY20 levels, while boosting factory productivity by 50% above the standards set at its flagship Manesar plant in Haryana, according to Toshihiro Suzuki, president of Suzuki Motor. "As a challenge to become a company that can keep pace with the speed of change, while halving the new model development period, we will improve development efficiency by 30%, and increase production efficiency by 50%," Suzuki said at the company's Technology Strategy Briefing 2026 on Friday.

The shorter development cycle will change the way Suzuki makes vehicles. Instead of completing planning, design, production engineering, quality and procurement sequentially, these functions will work concurrently from the early stages of a vehicle programme. The company also plans to retain a multi-powertrain strategy and not rely solely on battery electric vehicles, Suzuki said.

He identified Japan and India as the key centres of the company's global business foundation, and said technologies developed in Japan will be shared with Maruti Suzuki India and adapted for individual markets.

India will be strengthened as a manufacturing and export hub, he added. The company is targeting commissioning annual production capacity of 4 million vehicles in India from FY30, up from 2.9 million units now. Output was recently boosted by a fourth production line at Hansalpur, Gujarat, which brought that facility's annual capacity to 1 million units. Maruti Suzuki, which has plants in Gurgaon, Manesar and Kharkhoda, is planning to have a new site in Sanand. Suzuki also plans to deepen digital engineering and expand modularisation, allowing modules to be shared across products and integrating development and manufacturing more closely.

title: Suzuki Planning to Halve Auto Development Time
